chunks: They are the people of this world, turning towards it,
and hastening to it, and they have known justice, seen it, heard it, and appreciated it,
and they knew that people are equal in our view in the matter of right,
so they fled to selfishness and partiality,
far are they from it and remote!

key_terms.بُعْداً: far/remote (a term of curse or distance)

ai.seo_question: Why did the defectors to Syria flee from justice according to Imam Ali in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) critiques the defectors to Syria for abandoning the principle of *al-'adl* (justice) in favor of *al-athara* (partiality/preference), a key political theme in the early Shia understanding of governance. He emphasizes that their knowledge of justice was insufficient to guide their actions, as they actively chose worldly allure over the egalitarian standard set by the Imams, resulting in a divine curse (*subuha*). This reflects the Shia scholarly view that true leadership requires not just knowledge of truth, but the courage to implement it without bias.

en.sayed-ali-raza: They are seekers of this world and are proceeding to it and are leaping towards it.
They have known justice, seen it, heard it and appreciated it.
They have realized that here, to us, all men are equal in the matter of right.
Therefore, they ran away to selfishness and partiality.
Let them remain remote and far away.
